paragraphs: American Public Education, Inc., or APEI, provides online and campus-based postsecondary education to approximately 108,600 students through our subsidiary institutions. Our institutions offer purpose-built education programs designed to prepare individuals for productive contributions to their professions and society and to offer opportunities designed to advance students in their current professions or to help them prepare for their next career.

Our vision is for education to transform lives, advance careers, and improve communities. Our mission is to Power Purpose, Potential and Prosperity for Those in Service to Others. Our institutions of advanced learning are purpose-built to prepare service-minded students for employment, careers, and leadership in a diverse and changing world. Many of our students are from underserved populations for whom our institutions can transform their and their families' lives. We are the number one educator of active-duty military and of veterans through American Public University System. We are a national leader in pre-licensure nursing education, focused on a Diploma in Practical Nursing, or PN diploma, and an Associate Degree in Nursing, or ADN, through Rasmussen University and Hondros College of Nursing, as well as a Bachelor of Science in Nursing, or BSN degree, through Rasmussen University.
We have three subsidiary institutions: American Public University System; Rasmussen University; and Hondros College of Nursing.

American Public University System, or APUS, provides online postsecondary education to approximately 88,700 adult learners. APUS traces its roots to American Military University, or AMU, which was founded in 1991, as a distance-learning, graduate-level institution for military officers seeking an advanced degree in military studies. Since then, APUS has broadened its focus to include veterans, extended military families, and other public service and service-minded communities, with a focus on educating those who serve. APUS has two brands: AMU, which is focused on educating students from the military and national security communities, and military families and veterans, and American Public University, or APU, which is focused on educating career-focused working adults with an emphasis on educating professionals working in service-minded communities, including nursing, public health, public administration, and business administration. Today, while the majority of APUS students are undergraduate-level, students are also enrolled in its certificate, graduate, and doctoral programs.

APUS is exclusively an online institution of higher learning, purpose-built to meet the needs of the communities it serves. Many of its students serve in positions requiring extended and irregular work schedules, are on-call for rapid response missions, participate in extended deployments and exercises, travel or relocate frequently, and often must balance family and work demands. Although APUS's focus has broadened since its founding, it continues to have an emphasis on its relationship with the military community. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 62% of APUS's students self-reported that they served in the military on active duty at the time of initial enrollment, and approximately 15% of APUS's students self-reported that they are a military veteran. The remainder of APUS's students are other military or military-affiliated professionals (such as reservists or National Guard members), family members of veterans and active-duty military and public service professionals (such as law enforcement personnel or other first responders) and other non-military students (such as working adult students).

APUS is institutionally accredited by The Higher Learning Commission, or HLC, an institutional accrediting agency recognized by the U.S. Department of Education, or ED. Most other higher education institutions accept APUS's courses for transfer credit as a result of this accreditation. For more details on APUS's HLC accreditation, see "Our Institutions and Operations – Our Institutions – Accreditation" and "Regulatory Environment – Accreditation – Institutional Accreditation" below.

RU provides nursing- and health sciences-focused postsecondary education to approximately 15,900 students at its 18 campuses across five states and online. Not included in these counts are the Green Bay, Wisconsin campus that was closed effective December 31, 2025, and the Wausau, Wisconsin campus, which RU intends to close on December 31, 2026. At the

beginning of its 125-year history, RU focused on educating business students to prepare them for practical careers in bookkeeping, secretarial services, and accounting. RU's foundation of education that transforms lives created an institution built to serve those not typically served by traditional higher education. While RU continues to offer programs across a broad range of study including business, technology, and education, it expanded its breadth and embarked on providing healthcare education in 2006. Today, RU offers a comprehensive "ladder" of nursing degrees, including a pre-licensure Diploma in PN, ADN, and BSN degree, as well as the post-licensure RN to BSN degree, Master of Science in Nursing degree and Doctorate of Nursing Practice. In addition, RU also offers a post-graduate nursing certificate.

RU is committed to innovation in program delivery. For example, virtually every nursing program at RU incorporates online content alongside lab and clinical or classroom components. As of December 31, 2025, on-ground enrollment was approximately 7,100 students, of which approximately 6,200 were pursuing nursing degrees at RU, approximately 90% of whom were enrolled in RU's pre-licensure nursing degree programs. At December 31, 2025, online enrollment was approximately 8,800 students.

RU is institutionally accredited by HLC with an Open Pathway designation, and all of RU's Nursing programs are programmatically accredited by specialty nursing accrediting bodies. As with APUS, most other higher education institutions accept RU's courses for transfer credit as a result of RU's HLC accreditation.

HCN provides nursing education to approximately 4,000 students at eight campuses across three states. HCN offers pre-licensure nursing programs that are designed to prepare individuals for productive careers through both a PN diploma and an ADN, and a Direct Entry ADN option that offer an accelerated graduation pathway for students who meet certain transfer credit, academic, and entrance exam requirements.

HCN's students principally receive on-campus instruction at one of HCN's campuses and online for certain courses for those that prefer remote course learning. As of December 31, 2025, approximately 68% of HCN students were enrolled in a PN program and 32% were enrolled in an ADN program.

HCN is institutionally accredited by the Accrediting Bureau of Health Education Schools, or ABHES, a national accrediting agency recognized by ED. HCN's PN program is accredited by the National League for Nursing Commission for Nursing Education Accreditation, or NLN CNEA.

For the periods covered by this Annual Report, we had three reportable segments: the APUS Segment; the RU Segment; and the HCN Segment. Unallocated corporate activity, eliminations, and GSUSA's results prior to the GSUSA Sale Date are included in "Corporate and Other" in the Consolidated Financial Statements. Financial information regarding each of our reportable segments is reported and discussed in this Annual Report in the sections entitled "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations". Beginning in fiscal year 2026, we will have two reportable segments: APU Global, formerly the APUS Segment, and RU Health+, the businesses that formerly comprised the RU Segment and HCN Segment.

headings: Risks Related to Attracting and Retaining Students
Our success and financial performance depend on the effectiveness of our ability to attract students who persist in our institutions' programs.
If we are unable to effectively market our programs or expand into new markets, our results of operations would be negatively affected.
Declines in enrollments at RU could have a material adverse effect on RU's and our profitability, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.
Continued strong competition in the postsecondary education market could decrease our institutions' market share and increase our cost of acquiring students.
We expect to continue to face greater competition from non-traditional offerings, provided by both educational institutions and non-traditional providers.
Tuition and fee increases at RU, APUS, and HCN could have an adverse impact on enrollment, our financial condition and our results of operations.
RU's actual and planned closure of campuses or termination of programs on certain campuses may adversely impact RU and us.
Risks Related to the Regulation of Our Industry

If our institutions fail to maintain their institutional accreditation, they will lose the ability to participate in Title IV, DoD TA programs, and VA programs and our student enrollments would decline.
If one or more of our institutions does not comply with the 90/10 Rule for two consecutive years, it or they will lose eligibility to participate in federal student financial aid programs.
HLC could identify deficiencies during its mid-cycle comprehensive evaluation of APUS and take adverse action against APUS based on such deficiencies.
ED's gainful employment requirements could materially and adversely affect our business.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. Before making an investment, you should carefully consider the following risks, as well as the other information contained in this Annual Report, including our "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations". Any of the risk factors described below could significantly and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and prospects. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe are not material may also adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, and prospects. As a result of the risks and uncertainties described below, as well as such additional risks and uncertainties, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment.

Building awareness and reputation among potential students of our institutions and the programs they offer is critical to our institutions' ability to attract new students. In order to maintain and increase our revenue, profits, and cash flows, our institutions must continue to enroll new, qualified students in a cost-effective manner, and these students must remain active and be successful in our institutions' programs. In addition, because our institutions experience declines in their student populations as a result of graduation, transfers to other academic institutions, withdrawals, military deployments, and other reasons, in order to grow, we need to first attract sufficient students to replace those who have left. In addition to broader challenges with attracting qualified students, any negative effects resulting from the occurrence of risks set forth in this "Risk Factors" section, from action or inaction by us, regulators or accrediting agencies, or events beyond our control could prevent us from successfully advertising and marketing our institutions' programs and from successfully enrolling and retaining qualified students in those programs. If we are unable to continue to develop awareness and a positive reputation of our institutions and the programs we offer, and to recruit and enroll students that persist in our programs over time, our enrollments will suffer and there could be a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

Our marketing strategy for APUS has traditionally focused on building long-term, mutually beneficial relationships with businesses, other organizations, and individuals in military, veterans, extended military families, and other public service and service-minded communities, with a focus on educating those who serve. We must continue to develop and expand marketing channels that attract college-ready students who use non-federal funds as a payment source and may perform well at APUS, including in order to maintain compliance with the 90/10 Rule. However, we have experienced challenges attracting such students, and there is no assurance that we will be able to do so on a cost-effective basis or to prevent declines in these types of enrollments at APUS.

Furthermore, because APUS's tuition is generally lower than that of most of its competitors, it has fewer dollars to spend per student on marketing and advertising than its competitors. Our pricing structure and margin profile may limit the availability of financial resources to be used for marketing and enrollment in general. Nevertheless, we have tried to, and may in the future try to, implement new marketing tactics and channels, including those with which we have no experience, and there is no guarantee that our marketing and branding efforts will achieve the desired results. If we are unable to develop and optimize marketing and advertising programs that are effective in developing awareness of our institutions and the programs we offer and their value propositions, and we are unable to enroll and retain qualified students in the markets we serve, our enrollments would suffer, and there could be a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

In April 2024, APU announced its intention to expand its reach to become a global digital university that integrates emerging technologies and enhanced teaching and learning opportunities for faculty and students, adopted a new visual identity, a new tagline: Digital Learning for Real LifeTM, an expanded global focus, and a suite of digital student services. In connection with this transition, APU aims to provide students with highly collaborative learning experiences, AI-powered classroom support, and personalized digital services. This transition and rebranding initiative may be difficult to complete, divert management attention, and require us to expend resources and incur expenses. Additionally, despite APU's efforts, this transition and rebranding initiative may not yield increased enrollments, and, even if it does, any increased enrollments may not offset expenses we incur and could potentially impact the mix of students attracted to APU, which could have a negative effect on our compliance with the 90/10 Rule. If APU fails to successfully transition into a global digital university or incurs substantial

expenses in an unsuccessful attempt to do so, we may fail to attract new enrollments to the extent necessary to realize a sufficient return on our efforts. Accordingly, our business, results of operations, and financial condition could be impacted.

paragraphs: You should read the following discussion together with the consolidated financial statements and the related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report. This discussion contains forward-looking statements that are based on management's current expectations, estimates, and projections about our business and operations, and involves risks and uncertainties. Our actual results may differ materially from those currently anticipated and expressed in such forward-looking statements as a result of a number of factors, including those we discuss under "Risk Factors", "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements", and elsewhere in this Annual Report. For a discussion of our financial condition and results of operations for 2024 compared to 2023, refer to Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC, on March 6, 2025, which discussion is incorporated in this Annual Report by reference and which is available free of charge on the SECs website at www.sec.gov.

We are a provider of online and campus-based postsecondary education to approximately 108,600 students through three subsidiary institutions, American Public University System, or APUS, Rasmussen University, or RU, and Hondros College of Nursing, or HCN. Our subsidiary institutions offer purpose-built education programs designed to prepare individuals for productive contributions to their professions and society, and offer opportunities designed to advance students in their current professions or to help them prepare for their next career. Our subsidiary institutions are licensed or otherwise authorized by state authorities to offer postsecondary education programs to the extent the institutions believe such licenses or authorizations are required and are certified by ED to participate in Title IV programs. Additional information regarding our subsidiary institutions and their regulation is included in the "Business" section of this Annual Report.

Our revenue is largely driven by the number of students enrolled at our institutions, the number of and types of courses that students take, student payor source, and the mix of programs students attend. Our consolidated revenue in 2025 was $648.9 million, representing a $24.3 million, or 3.9%, increase from $624.6 million in 2024. This includes revenue from GSUSA through July 25, 2025, or the GSUSA Sale Date. A significant portion of our revenue comes from our institutions' participation in Title IV programs, and APUS's participation in the DoD TA programs, and VA education programs, and this creates significant risks to our operations.
Our operations for the periods covered by this Annual Report are organized into three reporting segments:
•American Public University System, or APUS Segment. This segment reflects the operational activities of APUS.
•Rasmussen University Segment, or RU Segment. This segment reflects the operational activities of RU.
•Hondros College of Nursing Segment, or HCN Segment. This segment reflects the operational activities of HCN.
Beginning in fiscal year 2026, we will have two reporting segments: APU Global, formerly the APUS Segment, and RU Health+, the business that formerly comprised the RU Segment and HCN Segment.

On January 28, 2025, we announced the planned combination of APUS, RU, and HCN, or the Combination, which will result in a combined institution named American Public University System comprised of two divisions named (i) APU Global, comprised of AMU and APU, and (ii) RU Health+, comprised of RU's campus-based and online nursing programs, RU's healthcare programs, HCN's campus-based nursing and healthcare programs, and RU's non-healthcare programs. The Combination constitutes a Change of Control, Structure or Organization pursuant to HLC policy and, accordingly, we were required to obtain HLC approval prior to effectuating the Combination. In December 2024, APUS and RU jointly submitted an application for Change of Control, Structure or Organization to HLC. Subsequently, ED informed us that we would need to follow a different process to implement the Combination that entails two steps instead of one: (i) merger of the legal entities that own and operate APUS, RU, and HCN, with the APUS entity surviving following the merger, and (ii) combination of the institutions into one HLC-accredited institution. As a result of this process change, HLC required APUS and RU to submit a new joint application for Change of Control, Structure or Organization to HLC in September 2025 containing substantially the same information that had been submitted previously and reflecting the two-step process. In February 2026, HLC approved the continuation of accreditation of APUS and RU after the legal entity merger with an acknowledgment that the intent is to eventually consolidate the three institutions into one HLC accreditation. ABHES has also informed HCN that it will continue HCN's ABHES accreditation after the legal entity merger. On March 2, 2026, we completed the merger of the legal entities that

own and operate APUS, RU, and HCN with the APUS entity surviving the merger, and subsequently notified ED that the merger occurred and resulted in RU and HCN being directly owned by the same legal entity that directly owns APUS. We currently expect to complete the implementation of step two of the Combination in the third quarter of 2026, subject to obtaining required approvals. We will evaluate changes to our segment reporting as a result of the Combination. For the years ended December 31, 2024, and 2025, we incurred $2.2 million and $3.5 million in professional fees, respectively, and we expect to incur between approximately $2.0 million and $4.0 million in professional fees in 2026 to complete the Combination. See the Risk Factor with the caption beginning "The planned combination of APUS, RU, and HCN …" and "Business – Regulatory Environment – Accreditation – Institutional Accreditation – The Planned Combination of APUS, RU, and HCN" for more information.

U.S. Federal Government Shutdown. On October 1, 2025, the U.S. federal government shut down due to a failure by Congress to pass appropriations legislation, resulting in, among other things, suspension of the DoD TA programs and ultimately an inability of APUS students seeking to use TA as a payment source to register, or in some cases stay registered, for courses. The 2025 Shutdown ended on November 12, 2025.

In connection with the 2025 Shutdown, APUS TA course registrations decreased by approximately 20,600 in the fourth quarter 2025, when compared to the prior year period. This was the first time since 2013 that APUS had dropped course registrations as a result of a government shutdown because the Defense Appropriations Bill, which annually funds TA, was not passed before the 2025 Shutdown.

Prior to the end of the 2025 Shutdown, on October 24, 2025, the Navy announced that TA funding was restored for classes starting on or before December 31, 2025, using TA funds appropriated as part of the OBBBA, or OBBBA TA Funds. Also, prior to the end of the 2025 Shutdown, certain individuals responsible for oversight of the voluntary education programs at the Army, Air Force, Navy, and Marines returned to their roles and, in the cases of the Army, Air Force, and Navy, began approving TA requests using OBBBA TA Funds. As of November 10, 2025, APUS estimated that it was able to recover approximately 5,000 course registrations for November 2025 course starts by students using OBBBA TA funds. As a result of the 2025 Shutdown, we implemented various cost savings measures, including a reduction in force, hiring freeze, and a reduction in travel and discretionary costs.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act. As discussed in "Business –Regulatory Actions and Restrictions on Operations – Other Regulations – The One Big Beautiful Bill Act", President Trump recently signed into law the OBBBA, which, among other things, makes significant changes to federal student financial aid programs and related eligibility requirements. New caps on federal loans may limit borrowing options for our students and a new accountability framework could limit the availability of certain programs due to a potential loss of Direct Loans, which could have a significant adverse impact on enrollments and our business, operations, and financial results. See "Risk Factors – Risks Related to the Regulation of Our Industry – "The One Big Beautiful Bill Act . . . ." for additional information regarding risks relating to the OBBBA.

paragraphs: American Public Education, Inc., or APEI, 提供線上及校園式後續教育，服務約 108,600 名學生，透過我們的子公司機構。我們的機構提供專為教育設計的課程，旨在協助個人為其專業與社會做出具生產力的貢獻，並提供機會協助學生在現有專業中進步或準備下一階段的職涯。

我們的願景是教育能改變人生、促進職涯發展與改善社區。我們的使命是為服務他人者提供力量、潛能與繁榮。我們的高階教育機構專為培訓具服務心態的學生，使其能在多元且變動的社會中就業、發展職涯與領導能力。許多我們的學生來自被忽略的羣體，我們的機構能改變他們及其家庭的生活。我們是美國現役軍人與退伍軍人教育的領導者，透過 American Public University System。我們在預許可護理教育方面為國家領導者，專注於實用護理文憑（PN 文憑）與護理副學士學位（ADN）的教育，透過 Rasmussen University 和 Hondros College of Nursing，以及透過 Rasmussen University 提供護理科學學士學位（BSN）。
我們有三個子公司機構：American Public University System；Rasmussen University；以及 Hondros College of Nursing。

American Public University System, or APUS, 提供線上後續教育，服務約 88,700 名成人學習者。APUS 的起源可追溯至 American Military University, or AMU，該機構於 1991 年成立，作為一個遠距學習的研究生機構，專為尋求軍事研究高階學位的軍官而設。自那之後，APUS 的重點已擴展至退伍軍人、擴展軍事家庭，以及其他公共服務與具服務心態的社羣，專注於教育那些為社會服務的人士。APUS 有兩個品牌：AMU，專注於教育來自軍事與國家安全社羣的學生，以及軍事家庭與退伍軍人；以及 American Public University, or APU，專注於教育具職涯導向的成人學習者，強調教育在具服務心態社羣中工作的專業人士，包括護理、公共衛生、公共行政與企業管理。

APUS 是一個專為服務其社羣而設計的 exclusively 線上高等教育機構。許多學生在需要延長與不規則工作時程的職位上服務，需隨時待命以應對快速反應任務，參與延長部署與演習，頻繁旅行或遷移，並經常必須平衡家庭與工作需求。雖然 APUS 自成立以來的重點已擴展，但其仍持續強調與軍事社羣的關係。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約 62% 的 APUS 學生自述在入學時為現役軍人，約 15% 的 APUS 學生自述為退伍軍人。APUS 的其餘學生為其他軍事或與軍事相關的專業人士（如預備役或國民警衛隊成員）、退伍軍人與現役軍人家庭成員及公共服務專業人士（如執法人員或其他第一線應急人員）以及非軍事學生（如工作成人學生）。

APUS 經過 The Higher Learning Commission, or HLC 認證，HLC 是美國教育部，or ED 承認的機構認證機構。大多數其他高等教育機構因這個認證而接受 APUS 的課程作為轉學學分。如需更多關於 APUS 的 HLC 認證資訊，請參閱下方的 "Our Institutions and Operations – Our Institutions – Accreditation" 以及 "Regulatory Environment – Accreditation – Institutional Accreditation"。
RU 在其位於五個州的 18 個校區與線上，提供約 15,900 名學生專注於護理與健康科學的後續教育。這些數字不包含於 2025 年 12 月 31 日關閉的 Wisconsin Green Bay 校區，以及 RU 計畫於 2026 年 12 月 31 日關閉的 Wisconsin Wausau 校區。

在 RU 125 年的歷史開始時，RU 專注於教育商務學生，使其為會計、祕書服務與簿記等實用職涯做準備。RU 的教育理念，即改變人生，創造了一個為傳統高等教育通常未服務的羣體而設的機構。雖然 RU 仍提供涵蓋商業、科技與教育等廣泛領域的課程，但於 2006 年擴展其範疇，並開始提供醫療照護教育。今天，RU 提供一整套的護理學位，包括預許可的 PN 文憑、ADN 學位與 BSN 學位，以及後許可的 RN 到 BSN 學位、護理科學碩士學位與護理實踐博士學位。此外，RU 也提供後碩士護理證書。
RU 以創新方式提供課程。例如，RU 的幾乎所有護理課程均包含線上內容與實驗室及臨牀或課堂零組件。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，實體課程註冊學生約為 7,100 人，其中約 6,200 人正在修讀 RU 的護理學位，約 90% 的學生修讀的是 RU 的預許可護理學位課程。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，線上課程註冊學生約為 8,800 人。
RU 經機構認證由 HLC 認證，並具有 Open Pathway 認證資格，且 RU 的所有護理課程均經專門護理認證機構認證。如同 APUS，大多數其他高等教育機構因 RU 的 HLC 認證而接受 RU 的課程作為轉學學分。
HCN 在三個州的八個校區為約 4,000 名學生提供護理教育。HCN 提供預許可護理課程，旨在透過 PN 文憑與 ADN，以及 Direct Entry ADN 選項，為個人準備具生產力的職業，後者為符合特定轉學學分、學術及入學考試要求的學生提供加速畢業途徑。
HCN 的學生主要在 HCN 的校區接受實體課程，並針對偏好遠距學習的學生提供部分課程的線上教學。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，約 68% 的 HCN 學生修讀 PN 課程，32% 修讀 ADN 課程。
HCN 經機構認證由 Accrediting Bureau of Health Education Schools，或 ABHES，一家被 ED 承認的國家認證機構認證。HCN 的 PN 課程經 National League for Nursing Commission for Nursing Education Accreditation，或 NLN CNEA 認證。

在本年度報告涵蓋的期間，我們有三個應報告分部：APUS 分部、RU 分部與 HCN 分部。未分配的公司活動、抵銷項目及 GSUSA 在 GSUSA 銷售日之前的結果包含於「公司及其他」項目中，於合併財務報表中。關於各應報告分部的財務資訊於本年度報告的「財務報表與補充資料」及「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析」部分進行報告與討論。自 2026 年會計年度起，我們將有兩個應報告分部：APU Global，原為 APUS 分部，以及 RU Health+，原為 RU 分部與 HCN 分部的業務。

paragraphs: 你應閱讀下列討論內容，並與本年度財務報表及相關附註說明一併參考。本討論內容包含前瞻性陳述，這些陳述是基於管理階層目前對本公司業務與運作的預期、估計與預測，並涉及風險與不確定性。本公司實際結果可能與目前預期及表達於這些前瞻性陳述之內容有重大差異，原因包括我們在「風險因素」、「前瞻性陳述特別說明」及其他部分所討論的多項因素。有關本公司 2024 年財務狀況與營運結果與 2023 年比較的討論，請參閱本公司於 2025 年 3 月 6 日向 SEC 提交的 10-K 年度報告，第 II 部分第 7 項，該討論內容已於本年度報告中引用，且可免費於 SEC 網站 www.sec.gov 取得。

本公司為約 108,600 名學生提供線上及校園式後續教育，透過三個子公司機構，即美國公開大學系統（American Public University System，或 APUS）、拉森大學（Rasmussen University，或 RU）以及洪德斯護理學院（Hondros College of Nursing，或 HCN）。我們的子公司機構提供專為教育設計的課程，以協助個人為其專業與社會做出具生產力的貢獻，並提供機會協助學生在現有職業中進步，或為其下個職涯做準備。我們的子公司機構在符合機構認為所需的情況下，已取得州政府的許可或授權，提供後續教育課程，並經 ED 認證參與 Title IV 計畫。有關我們子公司機構及其規範的更多資訊，請參閱本年度報告的「業務」部分。

我們的營業收入主要由機構 enrolment 的學生數量、學生修讀課程的數量與類型、學生付款來源以及學生修讀課程的組合所驅動。我們 2025 年的合併營業收入為 648.9 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 624.6 百萬美元增加 24.3 百萬美元，或成長 3.9%。此數字包含 GSUSA 透過 2025 年 7 月 25 日（GSUSA Sale Date）的營業收入。我們營業收入的很大一部分來自機構參與 Title IV 計畫，以及 APUS 參與 DoD TA 計畫與 VA 教育計畫，這會對我們的運作造成重大風險。
本年度報告所涵蓋期間的運作，已劃分為三個應報告分部：
•美國公開大學系統（American Public University System，或 APUS 分部）。此分部反映 APUS 的運作活動。
•拉森大學分部（Rasmussen University Segment，或 RU 分部）。此分部反映 RU 的運作活動。
•洪德斯護理學院分部（Hondros College of Nursing Segment，或 HCN 分部）。此分部反映 HCN 的運作活動。
自財務年度 2026 年起，我們將有兩個應報告分部：APU Global（原為 APUS 分部），以及 RU Health+（原為 RU 分部與 HCN 分部所組成的業務）。

於 2025 年 1 月 28 日，我們宣佈預計將 APUS、RU 與 HCN 進行合併，或稱為 Combination，此合併後將成立一個名為 American Public University System 的機構，包含兩個部門，分別為 (i) APU Global，包含 AMU 與 APU，以及 (ii) RU Health+，包含 RU 的校內與線上護理課程、RU 的醫療相關課程、HCN 的校內護理與醫療相關課程，以及 RU 的非醫療相關課程。此 Combination 屬於 HLC 政策所定義的 Change of Control、Structure 或 Organization，因此我們在執行此 Combination 前必須取得 HLC 的批准。於 2024 年 12 月，APUS 與 RU 共同向 HLC 提交 Change of Control、Structure 或 Organization 的申請。隨後，ED 告知我們，我們需要遵循一個不同的程序來執行此 Combination，此程序包含兩個步驟，而非一個步驟：(i) 合併擁有並運作 APUS、RU 與 HCN 的法律實體，且 APUS 實體在合併後繼續存續，以及 (ii) 將這些機構組合成一個 HLC 認證的機構。由於此程序的變更，HLC 要求 APUS 與 RU 在 2025 年 9 月向 HLC 提交一個新的共同申請，內容與先前提交的資訊幾乎相同，並反映此兩步驟的程序。於 2026 年 2 月，HLC 批准 APUS 與 RU 在法律實體合併後繼續取得認證，並承認其意圖最終將這三個機構合併為一個 HLC 認證機構。ABHES 也已告知 HCN，其 ABHES 認證將在法律實體合併後繼續有效。於 2026 年 3 月 2 日，我們完成了擁有並運作 APUS、RU 與 HCN 的法律實體的合併

本公司擁有並營運APUS、RU及HCN，APUS實體在合併後存續，隨後已通知ED合併已發生，且RU及HCN直接由與直接擁有APUS之同一法律實體所有。本公司目前預期於2026年第三季完成合併第二階段之實施，以取得所需核准為前提。本公司將評估因合併而導致之應報告分部變更。截至2024年12月31日及2025年12月31日止之會計年度，本公司分別產生2.2百萬美元及3.5百萬美元之專業費用，並預期於2026年產生約2.0百萬至4.0百萬美元之專業費用以完成合併。有關更多資訊，請參閱標題為「APUS、RU及HCN之預計合併…」之風險因素，以及「業務 – 規管環境 – 認證 – 機構認證 – APUS、RU及HCN之預計合併」。
美國聯邦政府停擺。2025年10月1日，因國會未能通過撥款法案，導致美國聯邦政府停擺，造成包括國防部TA計畫暫停在內之多項影響，最終導致APUS學生無法使用TA作為付款來源註冊或在某些情況下維持註冊修讀課程。2025年停擺於2025年11月12日結束。
因應 2025 年停擺事件，APUS TA 課程註冊人數在 2025 年第四季減少約 20,600 人，與前一年同期相比。這是自 2013 年以來，APUS 首次因政府停擺導致課程註冊人數下降，因為 defence appropriations bill，該法案每年資助 TA，未在 2025 年停擺前通過。

在 2025 年停擺結束前，2025 年 10 月 24 日，海軍宣佈 TA 資金已恢復，用於 2025 年 12 月 31 日前開始的課程，使用 OBBBA 資助的 TA 資金，或 OBBBA TA 資金。同時，在 2025 年停擺結束前，負責陸軍、空軍、海軍及海軍陸戰隊志願教育計畫監督的某些人員已返回其職務，並在陸軍、空軍及海軍的情況下，開始使用 OBBBA TA 資金核准 TA 請求。截至 2025 年 11 月 10 日，APUS 預估可透過 OBBBA TA 資金恢復約 5,000 名學生於 2025 年 11 月課程的註冊人數。因應 2025 年停擺事件，我們實施了多項節省成本措施，包括裁員、凍結招聘以及減少出差及酌情開支。

一項大而美麗的法案。如「業務 – 規管行動與營運限制 – 其他規範 – 一項大而美麗的法案」所討論，總統川普最近已簽署 OBBBA 成為法律，該法案除其他事項外，對聯邦學生財務援助計畫及相關資格要求做出重大變更。新的聯邦貸款上限可能限制學生的貸款選擇，而新的責任架構可能因潛在的 Direct Loans 損失，限制某些計畫的可用性，這可能對註冊人數及我們的業務、營運與財務結果造成重大負面影響。請參閱「風險因素 – 與產業規管相關的風險 – 一項大而美麗的法案 ……」以取得更多與 OBBBA 相關的風險資訊。

headings: 與吸引及留住學生相關的風險
本公司之成功與財務表現取決於本公司吸引學生持續參與本機構課程之能力有效性。
若本公司無法有效行銷其課程或拓展至新市場，將對本公司之營運結果產生負面影響。
RU 學生報名人數下降可能對 RU 及本公司之獲利能力、財務狀況、營運結果及現金流產生重大不利影響。
後續教育市場持續強烈競爭可能降低本公司機構之市場佔有率，並提高本公司獲取學生之成本。
本公司預期將持續面臨來自教育機構及非傳統提供者之非傳統課程所提供之更大競爭。
RU、APUS 及 HCN 之學費及費用提高可能對學生報名人數、本公司之財務狀況及營運結果產生負面影響。
RU 實際或計畫關閉校區或終止特定校區之課程可能對 RU 及本公司產生不利影響。
與我們產業規範相關的風險
若我方機構未能維持其機構認證資格，將喪失參與 Title IV、DoD TA 計畫及 VA 計畫之資格，導致我方學生入學人數減少。
若我方任一機構連續兩年未能符合 90/10 規則，該機構將喪失參與聯邦學生財務補助計畫之資格。
HLC 可能在其中期全面評估 APUS 時發現缺失，並基於此缺失對 APUS 採取不利措施。
教育部的就業收益要求可能對我方業務造成重大且不利的影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。在進行投資前，您應謹慎考慮下列風險，以及本年度報告中包含的其他資訊，包括我們的「財務會計與補充資料」及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」。任何上述風險因素均可能顯著且不利地影響我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流及前景。上述所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們唯一面臨的風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不具重大性，也可能不利地影響我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果、現金流及前景。因此，因應上述所描述的風險與不確定性，以及這些其他風險與不確定性，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。

在潛在學生羣體中建立我們機構與其所提供課程的認知與聲譽，對我們機構吸引新學生的能力至關重要。為維持並增加我們的收入、利潤與現金流，我們機構必須持續以成本效益的方式招收新且合格的學生，且這些學生必須持續參與並在機構的課程中表現成功。此外，由於我們機構因畢業、轉學至其他教育機構、退學、軍事部署及其他原因，學生人數會減少，為實現成長，我們首先需要吸引足夠的學生以取代已離去的學生。除了吸引合格學生的廣泛挑戰外，任何因本「風險因素」部分所述風險事件發生、我們或監管機構及認證機構的作為或不作為，或我們無法控制的事件所導致的負面影響，都可能阻止我們成功宣傳與行銷我們機構的課程，並成功招收與留住這些課程的合格學生。若我們無法持續建立我們機構與所提供課程的認知與正面聲譽，並招募與招收能持續參與我們課程的學生，我們的招生數量將受到影響，且可能對我們的財務狀況與營運結果造成重大不利影響。

我們對APUS的行銷策略傳統上著重於與軍事、退伍軍人、擴展軍事家庭及其他公共服務與服務導向社羣中的企業、其他組織及個人建立長期且互利的關係，重點在於教育那些服務於國家的人士。我們必須持續發展並擴展能吸引使用非聯邦資金作為付款來源且可能在APUS表現良好的大學準備學生的行銷管道，包括以維持符合90/10規則。然而，我們已面臨吸引這些學生的挑戰，且無法保證我們能以成本效益的方式做到這一點，或能防止APUS這類招生數量的下降。

此外，因為 APUS 的學費通常低於其大部分競爭對手，因此其在每位學生身上用於行銷與廣告的預算較少。我們的定價結構與毛利率形態可能限制可用於行銷與招生的財務資源。儘管如此，我們已嘗試並可能在未來嘗試實施新的行銷策略與通路，包括我們目前沒有經驗的領域，但無法保證我們的行銷與品牌建設努力會達到預期的結果。若我們無法發展並優化有效的行銷與廣告方案，以提高我們機構與所提供的課程及其價值主張的知名度，且無法在所服務的市場中招收並留住合格學生，則我們的招生數量將受到影響，並可能對我們的財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。

2024 年 4 月，APU 宣佈其意圖擴大影響力，成為整合新興科技與提升教師與學生教學與學習機會的全球數位大學，採用新的視覺識別系統、新的標語：Digital Learning for Real LifeTM、擴大的全球關注點，以及一組數位學生服務。與此轉型相關，APU 希望為學生提供高度協作的學習體驗、AI 支援的課堂服務，以及個性化的數位服務。此轉型與品牌重塑計畫可能難以完成，分散管理層的注意力，並要求我們投入資源與產生費用。此外，儘管 APU 的努力，此轉型與品牌重塑計畫可能不會增加招生數量，即使增加，任何增加的招生數量可能無法彌補我們所產生的費用，並可能影響吸引至 APU 的學生組成，這可能對我們符合 90/10 規則產生負面影響。若 APU 未能成功轉型為全球數位大學，或在失敗的嘗試中產生重大費用，我們可能無法吸引足夠的新招生以實現我們努力的足夠回報。
因此，我們的業務、營運成果與財務狀況可能受到影響。
